DesignID Overview

DesignID™ is a faith-integrated assessment that measures how individuals perceive how they reflect who God is. The four reflections used in this assessment are titled Architect, Artisan, Shepherd, and Steward. Each represents a reflection of how God works through human beings. Together, they help us better understand the following aspects of God: The Creator, Designer, Comforter, and Sustainer. The DesignID Assessment quantifies an individual’s preferences across these four aspects.

Vision: To help every believer discover, develop, and deploy their God-given design, equipping the Church to flourish through unity, diversity, and purpose.

DYDD + DesignID gives individuals a tangible way to live out the DYDD anchor verse:
“For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.” (Ephesians 2:10)

Biblical Foundation

  • Genesis 1:27 — We were created to reflect who God is.
  • 1 Peter 2:9 — Identity flows from whose we are, not who we are.
  • 1 Corinthians 15:10 — Grace does not just forgive; it fuels, sustains, and directs.
  • Galatians 5:16–17 — We are to operate in grace, not selfishness.

DesignID operationalizes these biblical truths into a practical assessment that quantifies how individuals reflect God’s image through creating (Architect), designing (Artisan), comforting (Shepherd), and sustaining (Steward).

Primary & Secondary Reflections

Your reflections reveal the unique ways God’s design comes alive through you. Your primary reflection ({{ Primary | default: '' }}) expresses your most natural way of reflecting God, the place where your efforts feel the most comfortable. Your secondary reflection ({{ Secondary | default: '' }}) complements and refines your primary, adding depth, balance, and perspective to how you live out your calling. Together, these reflections form an awareness of God’s grace at work in your life. When these two work together, they produce your integrative reflection ({{ Integrative_Reflection | default: '' }}), where a deeper purpose behind your design is revealed.

Integrative Reflection

Every person reflects four divine reflections (Architect, Artisan, Shepherd, and Steward) but few operate purely within one. Real life, leadership, and discipleship happen in the intersections between them. Integrative reflections reveal the six blended expressions of how we reflect God, the spaces where two reflections meet, creating unique character, insight, and calling.

Reflection Capacity

Every person carries the image of God, expressed through four reflections: Architect, Artisan, Shepherd, and Steward. But not every reflection carries the same range. Your design capacity describes how strongly God’s grace is currently flowing through each part of your divine design. It does not measure effort or ability but reveals where grace feels natural, steady, stretched, or strained.

In other words, capacity shows how God’s power moves through you; what gives life, what requires faith, and what invites rest. When your capacity is Abundant, you feel joy and ease; when it is Steady, you serve faithfully; when it is Limited, you depend intentionally on God; and when it is Drained, you learn surrender and partnership. Design capacity reminds us that His grace is always sufficient.

Each one should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God’s grace in its various forms. (1 Peter 4:10)

The Purpose of Capacity

  • Reveal natural grace flow: What comes easily, joyfully, and fruitfully.
  • Expose overused or undernourished energies: Where strain or fatigue may occur.
  • Support development and discipleship: Guiding self-awareness, leadership growth, and spiritual balance.
  • Honor divine diversity: Reminding us that no design is superior; each simply reflects a different grace intensity.

Capacity mirrors God’s relational approach with His people:

  • He gives Abundant grace to empower calling.
  • He sustains with Steady grace for endurance.
  • He teaches through Limited grace to cultivate dependence.
  • He redeems Drained grace by inviting rest and partnership.

Architect
(Creator) 		Visionary and faith-filled. You thrive when building, leading, or starting something new. Creation itself energizes you, where your faith comes alive. Reliable and strategic. You bring order and foresight to meaningful projects and lead confidently when goals are clear. Practical and structured but slower to initiate. You can plan effectively when prompted but may hesitate to start alone. Orderly but fatigued by decision-making. Too much pressure to lead or build drains clarity and joy.
Artisan
(Designer) 		Creative, insightful, and expressive. You bring beauty to truth and meaning to motion, revealing God’s wisdom through imagination. Consistent and thoughtful. You shape and refine ideas with care, balancing creativity and structure. Capable but cautious. You prefer clear frameworks and inspiration from others to stay engaged. Drained by repetition or rigid systems. When beauty feels buried by duty, your creativity dims.
Shepherd
(Comforter) 		Relational, empathetic, and encouraging. You nurture others toward growth and unity through patience and grace. Supportive and understanding. You provide steady care and dependable presence in relationships and teams. Caring but easily stretched. You show kindness yet need boundaries and rest to maintain empathy. Overextended by others’ needs. When compassion becomes striving, emotional fatigue follows.
Steward
(Sustainer) 		Faithful, organized, and dependable. You bring peace through order, ensuring excellence and integrity in all you oversee. Consistent and disciplined. You maintain stability and follow-through, supporting teams with quiet strength. Responsible but reluctant. You value order yet tire of long routines or endless details. Weary under constant obligation. When duty outweighs grace, your diligence turns to burden.

Shadow Reflection

Shadow reflections describe what happens when our divine design moves out of alignment with grace. They are not sin themselves, but rather the distractions, distortions, or divided attention that pull our reflection of God away from its intended purpose. When grace flows freely, we reflect His image clearly, but when pride, fear, or self-reliance interrupt that flow, our reflection bends toward self instead of service.

Shadows appear when the gift meant to bless becomes a burden we try to carry alone. Without awareness, these unguarded tendencies can mature into sin; control instead of courage, perfectionism instead of pursuit of excellence, people-pleasing instead of love.

Scripture reminds us, “If we claim to have fellowship with him and yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not live out the truth” (1 John 1:6). The purpose of identifying shadow reflections is therefore not condemnation but restoration, to recognize where light has dimmed. As Psalm 139:23–24 prays, “Search me, God, and know my heart…See if there is any offensive way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.”

On Purpose - For Purpose

“For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.”
(Ephesians 2:10)

Some people chase their calling like it’s a riddle to solve. Others wait for the perfect moment, hoping something big or dramatic will finally make life click. But what if the truth has been present the whole time? What if your divine design is already part of you, just waiting to be recognized?

Discover Your Divine Design is not another self-help formula. It is an invitation to uncover the truth of who you are and how you are made. This journey does not begin with what you do. It begins with who you are.

Discover Your Divine Design is a faith-based development program designed to help individuals and groups explore how God has uniquely created them to live with purpose. Grounded in Scripture and practical application, this journey walks through five key areas—your Identity, Expertise, Story, Desires, and Spiritual Gifts—to help you clearly understand your place in the Body of Christ (your Niche) and how you can serve with joy and confidence.

DYDD offers a growing collection of resources including books, courses, a spiritual gifts assessment, and more, all designed to support clarity, growth, and faithful action.

Introducing DesignPD

DesignPD helps you understand how you naturally Plan, Decide, and Do. Built on the foundation of DesignID, it brings your design into everyday life so you can see how your tendencies influence leadership, teamwork, decision making, and sustainable contribution.

“Commit to the Lord whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.”
Proverbs 16:3
